newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO SELL 30-40 SMALL FIRMS IN FAST-TRACK.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO SELL 30-40 SMALL FIRMS IN FAST-TRACK.

text.p: Poland's treasury ministry plans to sell between 30 and 40 small companies through simplified privatisation tender procedures, a deputy treasury minister said on Thursday.
"Last year, 20 companies were bought through this method. In 1997 we want to sell between 30 and 40 firms," Jozef Kowalczyk told a seminar.
He said interest in buying the companies, mostly supervised by provincial governments, was likely to increase in 1997 because payment for the firms could be made in instalments.
Last year the ministry planned to sell about 60 companies this way but interest proved small.

Under the simplified sell-off procedures, the ministry sets a minimum price for a company and asks investors for written offers, which are considered within weeks rather than months, as is the case with larger privatisations.
When choosing a buyer, the ministry will take into account the price, the size of the stake, promised investment, experience in the particular market and other factors.
